BoxScorePlayerOut.description: One player who played: has minutes, possibly zero seconds.
BoxScorePlayerOut.title: BoxScorePlayerOut

ChampionOut.description:
GET /events/seasons/{season}/champion. `result` is the Finals score,
the champion's wins first ("4-2"). All three are null until a team has
won four Finals games.
ChampionOut.title: ChampionOut

DataLinkOut.description: A stored attachment: `scope` is null except for a player_career.
DataLinkOut.title: DataLinkOut

DivisionStandingsOut.description: A division's teams, in their conference's order.
DivisionStandingsOut.title: DivisionStandingsOut

GameDetailOut.description:
GET /events/games/{id}: a read model built by
app.events.service.game_detail, not the ORM row.
GameDetailOut.title: GameDetailOut

GameFinalLink.description: A game's final score; `ref_id` is a games.id.
GameFinalLink.title: GameFinalLink

GameFinalPreviewView.description:
A game_final link's preview: every field of
app.events.service.GameFinalPreview.
GameFinalPreviewView.title: GameFinalPreviewView

LeaderOut.description:
`teams` are the abbreviations the player played for in the counted
games; `average` is per game, one place.
LeaderOut.title: LeaderOut

LeadersOut.description:
GET /events/seasons/{season}/leaders. `rule` names the qualifying
rule applied and `minimum_games` its minimum (0 for the playoffs).
LeadersOut.title: LeadersOut

MeOut.description:
Everything in PublicUserOut plus `date_of_birth` (PII) -- only ever
returned on a path that proves the caller is that profile's own owner
(`POST /users`, `GET /users/me`, `PATCH /users/me`), never on a path
another user can reach.
MeOut.title: MeOut

MediaStatus.description:
Linear state chain: UPLOADED -> SCANNING -> PROCESSED | REJECTED.
See app.media.state for the State pattern enforcing legal transitions.
MediaStatus.title: MediaStatus

NotificationType.description:
Closed set per wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x05-notifications.md
business rules -- `like` is explicitly excluded, not a 4th value
waiting to happen.
NotificationType.title: NotificationType

PlayerCareerLink.description: A player's career averages over one scope; `ref_id` is a players.id.
PlayerCareerLink.title: PlayerCareerLink

PlayerCareerPreviewView.description:
A player_career link's preview: every field of
app.events.service.PlayerCareerPreview, computed at read time, not a
snapshot from the post's creation; a scope with no games has null
averages.
PlayerCareerPreviewView.title: PlayerCareerPreviewView

PlayerDetailOut.description:
GET /events/players/{id}: a read model built by
app.events.service.player_detail. Only played rows of `regular` and
`playoffs` games count towards a line.
PlayerDetailOut.title: PlayerDetailOut

PlayerGameLink.description: A player's line in one game; `ref_id` is a player_game_stats.id.
PlayerGameLink.title: PlayerGameLink

PlayerGameOut.description:
One row of GET /events/players/{id}/games: the player's box-score
line in one game, played or not, with the game around it. A row
without minutes (`seconds_played` null) is a did-not-play.
PlayerGameOut.title: PlayerGameOut

PlayerGamePreviewView.description:
A player_game link's preview: every field of
app.events.service.PlayerGamePreview. A DNP line is as stored (null
seconds_played, its dnp_reason, zeros).
PlayerGamePreviewView.title: PlayerGamePreviewView

PostView.description:
feed/'s (and, per this unit's brief, search/'s) response shape for a
single post. Deliberately its own schema, not app.posts.schemas.PostOut
-- it carries fields (author, like_count, media, mentioned_game_ids)
PostOut doesn't, assembled from other modules' read interfaces rather
than the Post row alone.

`reply_count` counts direct replies, `repost_count` reposts plain and
quote, both leaving out soft-deleted authors. `reposted_by_viewer` is
whether the viewer has a *plain* repost of this post (false for a
guest). `reposted_post` is, on a repost, the view of the post it
reposts, one level deep (its own `reposted_post` is always null); null
on every other post and when the original is hidden.
`reposted_post_deleted` is true on a repost whose original its owner
deleted (its `reposted_post` is then null, and the client shows a "Post
deleted" placeholder); false everywhere else, including a repost whose
original is hidden only because its author is deactivated.

`data_link` is the post's own attachment in PostOut's shape (a plain
repost has none; its `reposted_post` carries the original's), and
`data_link_preview` that attachment's events/ preview: null without a
link, or when its target has no preview. Legacy EventMention rows
produce `mentioned_game_ids` only, never either field.
PostView.title: PostView

PublicUserOut.description:
Everything safe to return on the public, unauthenticated
`GET /users/{id}` profile-page read path -- "viewing other users'
account pages" is a public read path per wiki/CodeContext/Modules/
0x01-users.md Security section. No `date_of_birth` here -- see MeOut.
PublicUserOut.title: PublicUserOut

RecordEntryOut.description:
One entry of a ranked record list. `rank` is competition ranking
(equal values share a rank, the next rank skips). `team` is the team
(for a player's single-game record, the team they played for), null for
a player's count or career sum; `season` and `game` are null where the
record has none. `value` is an integer, except a season record's win
percentage (a fraction from 0 to 1, three places).
RecordEntryOut.title: RecordEntryOut

RecordGameOut.description: The game a single-game record was set in, and the opponent.
RecordGameOut.title: RecordGameOut

RecordHolderOut.description:
The list's first entry; `tied_count` is how many entries share its
value (1 when it is alone).
RecordHolderOut.title: RecordHolderOut

RecordListOut.description:
GET /events/records/{record_id}: one page of the record's top 100
entries. `total` is how many entries the list holds (at most 100).
RecordListOut.title: RecordListOut

RecordOut.description:
A team's regular-season record (only `regular` games count: NBA Cup
group and knockout games do; play-in, playoffs and the cup final do
not), with home and away splits.
RecordOut.title: RecordOut

RecordsSummaryOut.description:
GET /events/records. The data window is the earliest and latest
stored seasons, null when there are none.
RecordsSummaryOut.title: RecordsSummaryOut

SeasonLineOut.description:
One season and game type the player played in. `teams` are
abbreviations in the order first played; the stats are summed across
them, as nba.com's "TOT" row is.
SeasonLineOut.title: SeasonLineOut

ShootingOut.description:
Counting stats and shooting percentages, shared by a player's line
and a team's totals. Percentages are a fraction from 0 to 1, three
places, computed from made and attempted; null when none was attempted.
ShootingOut.title: ShootingOut

StandingRowOut.description:
`win_pct` is wins / games, three places. `games_behind` is in half
games behind the first team of the conference's order:
((leader_w - w) + (l - leader_l)) / 2.
StandingRowOut.title: StandingRowOut

StandingsOut.description:
GET /events/seasons/{season}/standings. `tie_break` names the
ordering rule: the NBA's own tie-breakers are not applied.
StandingsOut.title: StandingsOut

StatLineOut.description:
A career or season line: totals of the played rows, percentages
computed from the totals (the box score's rule) and per-game averages
to one place, null when no game was played.
StatLineOut.title: StatLineOut

TeamBoxScoreOut.description:
One team's side: played rows (starters first, then by seconds
played), the players who did not play, and totals summed from the
played rows, never adjusted to the final score.
TeamBoxScoreOut.title: TeamBoxScoreOut

TeamRefOut.description: A team as a game detail embeds it.
TeamRefOut.title: TeamRefOut

TeamSeasonGameOut.description: One of the team's games, from its side: `team_score` is its own.
TeamSeasonGameOut.title: TeamSeasonGameOut

TeamSeasonOut.description:
GET /events/teams/{team_id}/seasons/{season}: the regular-season
record and every game of every type, newest first.
TeamSeasonOut.title: TeamSeasonOut

ThreadView.description:
A post and its direct replies. `root` is null, and `root_deleted`
true, only when its owner deleted the root (POSTS-004): the surviving
replies stay readable under a "Post deleted" placeholder.
ThreadView.title: ThreadView

UpdateMeRequest.description:
`PATCH /users/me` body. Uses `model_fields_set` semantics (see
`app.users.service.update_profile`'s `fields_set` parameter): a field
absent from the request body is left untouched; a field present with an
explicit `null` clears it. `username`/`date_of_birth` are deliberately
not fields on this model -- neither is editable via this endpoint.
UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest

get.description:
One page, newest first (date, then id). Paged because a full load is
~30,000 games, over a Lambda response's 6 MB as one list (EVENTS-005).
Still a list, so the compose picker reads the 50 newest unchanged.

schema.title: Response List Games Events Games Get

get.description:
The game page: both teams, line scores and the box score per team.
posts/'s EventMention.game_id points here.

One page of players by last name, first name, id. `q` matches when
every word of it is a prefix of the first or last name, case- and
accent-insensitively; `season` keeps players who played in it.

schema.title: Response List Players Events Players Get

get.description:
The player page: attributes, regular-season and playoff career
lines, and one line per season and game type, newest first.
The player's game log, played and did-not-play, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Player Games Events Players  Player Id  Games Get

get.description:
Every historical record, team records then player records, each
with its rule and its holder: the first entry of its list and
`tied_count`, how many share that value; null when no stored data
qualifies. `since_season` and `through_season` are the stored data's
window. Cacheable: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

One page of a record's ranked list, which holds at most its top 100
entries (a tie at the 100th place is cut by the list's order); `total`
is how many it holds. Ordered by value (ascending for
team-worst-season, descending for every other), then date or season,
then id. Cacheable: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

404: an unknown record id. 422: `limit` outside 1-100 or `offset`
outside 0-99.

Every season with at least one stored game, of any type, newest
first, as "YYYY-YY".

schema.title: Response List Seasons Events Seasons Get

get.description:
The team that won four of the season's playoff games labelled "NBA
Finals", the runner-up and the series result. Until then all three are
null, in a 200.

422: a malformed season (not "YYYY-YY"). 404: a well-formed season with
no stored game.

The top players by per-game average of `stat` (`threes`: three-
pointers made) over their played games of `game_type`, then by player
id. Regular season: 65 games from 2023-24 on, before that 70 % of the
most games any team played, rounded up; the playoffs have no minimum.
The response names the rule and the minimum.

422: a malformed season, an unknown `stat` or `game_type`, or `limit`
outside 1-50. 404: a well-formed season with no stored game.

Regular-season standings by conference, then division. Within a
conference: win percentage, then wins, then team name (`tie_break`;
the NBA's own tie-breakers are not applied). Only `regular` games count.

422: a malformed season (not "YYYY-YY"). 404: a well-formed season with
no stored game.

No pagination — the NBA team set is ~30 rows, small and stable
(YAGNI, wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02-events.md).

schema.title: Response List Teams Events Teams Get

get.description:
One team's season: its regular-season record with home and away
splits, and every one of its games that season, of every type, newest
first.

422: a malformed season (not "YYYY-YY"). 404: an unknown team, or a
well-formed season with no stored game.

A root its owner deleted answers 200 with `root` null and its
surviving replies; a root hidden only by a deactivated author is 404,
as an unknown one is.

schema.title: Response Health Version Health Version Get

post.description:
A refused data_link (app.posts.data_link.DataLinkRefused) answers 422
with its machine code as the detail; a malformed one is Pydantic's own
422.

delete.description:
The owner's soft delete (app.posts.service.delete_post): 204, again
on a repeat; 403 for someone else's post; 409 for a plain repost, which
DELETE /posts/{original}/repost removes instead.

get.description:
404 for an unknown post and for one hidden by app.posts.service's
visibility rule (deleted, or its author deactivated).

Direct replies only, oldest first (natural thread reading order),
under the same visibility rule as the thread (app.posts.service.
replies_to). Returns an empty list both when the post has no replies
and when the post doesn't exist at all -- those two cases look the same
here, and that's fine (a caller who needs to know the post itself
exists already has GET /posts/{post_id} for that).

schema.title: Response List Replies Posts  Post Id  Replies Get

delete.description:
The undo: removes the caller's plain reposts of the post. 204
whether or not there was anything to remove; 409, removing nothing,
when one of them has a reply (or a repost) of its own.

409.description: A repost to remove is in use

post.description:
The one-click repost: 201 with the caller's new plain repost, or 200
with the one they already have (idempotent and race-free, see
app.posts.service.repost_post).

get.description:
Teams come from the existing GET /events/teams -- not duplicated
here, per wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x07-search.md.

schema.title: Response Get My Following Users Me Following Get
